issues.detail: The Hebrew 'וּכְפֹרֵפֵי זָהָב עֶשְׂרִים לַאֲדַרְכֹנִים אָלֶף' means 'and twenty gold bowls (or basins) worth a thousand darics' (i.e., twenty gold basins valued at a thousand darics). The Chinese renders '二十個金子的霜' which is unclear ('frost of gold'?) and does not convey 'bowls/basins' (כְּפוֹרִים). Also 'לַאֲדַרְכֹנִים אָלֶף' is 'worth a thousand darics' (a Persian coin), but the Chinese says '價值一千個德拉克馬' (worth a thousand drachmas), swapping the currency name from darics to drachmas, which is a factual change.
The Hebrew currency is 'אֲדַרְכֹנִים' (darics), but the Chinese uses '德拉克馬' (drachmas), a different currency, changing the historical reference.
